headline: High: firecrawl’s broad egress plus unstructured’s filesystem writes create default-path leakage and conflict risks; prompt-injection and cascading errors are also plausible via shared document content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API outputs, while unstructured reads and processes documents/images/text. If firecrawl output is fed into unstructured as trusted content, attacker-controlled markup or instructions can traverse the pair. The profiles do not prove a shared channel, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is copied into unstructured without sanitization, prompt-like instructions can influence downstream processing.
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or message queue, injected content can traverse automatically.
mitigations: Add a content-sanitization step before handing firecrawl output to unstructured.
Disable automatic instruction-following on parsed document text.
Use a provenance tag for all cross-agent inputs.
Review one sample payload for prompt-like strings before enabling the pipeline.

B_data_leakage.rationale: firecrawl touches API keys and has broad network egress; unstructured has filesystem read/write and processes documents. In a shared workspace, firecrawl-derived content or secrets can be written into files that unstructured reads and potentially uploads or transforms. The pair lacks explicit isolation guarantees, so the safer reading is high risk.
conditions: IF firecrawl stores scraped content or secrets in a directory unstructured can read, leakage becomes possible.
IF unstructured processes files containing API keys or sensitive web content, those data can be exposed in outputs or logs.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories.
Rotate any API keys used by firecrawl before testing the pair.
Restrict unstructured to a scratch folder with no secrets.
Inspect one output file for sensitive fields before enabling batch runs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: firecrawl supports multiple instances and broad API/network activity, while unstructured can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. Their write surfaces can overlap if orchestrated against the same workspace, creating race conditions or clobbered artifacts. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so the conflict is plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, files can be overwritten or partially read.
IF the orchestrator launches multiple instances without locks, concurrent mutations can race.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate output directory.
Enable file locking in the orchestrator.
Run one dry-run with a single document to check for collisions.
Rename outputs with unique run IDs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data, and unstructured is a document-processing pipeline that may treat upstream text as authoritative input. If firecrawl extracts a bad fact or malformed document, unstructured can propagate it into downstream artifacts without a verification step. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF unstructured consumes firecrawl output without validation, upstream extraction errors will cascade.
IF downstream automation trusts unstructured outputs, a single bad scrape can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between the agents.
Compare one extracted record against the source page manually.
Require schema checks on firecrawl output before ingestion.
Limit the first run to a small sample set.

E_compliance.rationale: firecrawl explicitly handles API keys and web content, while unstructured processes documents, images, and text. If regulated or personal data is scraped by firecrawl and then persisted or transformed by unstructured, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No certification or DPA details are provided for either agent, so compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is scraped by firecrawl and stored by unstructured, retention policy mismatch can occur.
IF the deployment requires a specific residency or certification, the profiles do not show matching controls.
mitigations: Classify the data before routing it between agents.
Delete intermediate files after processing.
Check the vendor privacy pages before production use.
Keep regulated datasets out of the pair until controls are confirmed.
